comment: Reviewed exemptions for the duplication gate (G17), applied only by a human. Four row kinds (#175): an L0 row {"fingerprint": "<12-hex from the L0 red>", "reason": "..."} accepts one token window by content fingerprint, so it stays accepted after it moves lines; an exact or near row {"fingerprint", "rule": "exact" | "near", "members": ["<subject>", ...], "reason"} accepts the exact class, or the near-miss pair, whose members are exactly those subjects, so a third copy is never covered; a mirror row {"mirror": ["<pathA>", "<pathB>"], "reason"} accepts a match between the file at one relative path on each side of a deliberate dual implementation; and a wire row {"fingerprint": "<key12>", "rule": "<wire check>", "members", "reason"} accepts one wire binding for the step that owns the rule. A new-kind row's reason is at least 20 characters. Write-guard-protected and listed in check-gate-integrity's ESCAPE_LISTS: an agent stages harness-proposals/<id>.json and a human applies it, and the commit appears in the PR diff under CODEOWNERS. The seeded rows below are the web/native design-system mirror, the two surfaces' i18n catalogs, and the two credential forms. Everything else must be extracted, not exempted.

allow.reason: packages/design-system/src vs packages/design-system-native/src — the deliberate web/native mirror, the ONE deliberate dual implementation in the scaffold. The two design systems share a variant CONTRACT (identical component, variant and option names, so a feature can move a screen between surfaces) but cannot share an implementation: web is Tailwind v4, mobile is Tailwind v3 via NativeWind 4, and the two majors do not share a class vocabulary. React Native has no cascade and no pseudo-classes, so the web's `focus-visible:` / `placeholder:` / `disabled:` variants become props and conditional classes on the native side, and its box model differs (RN flex defaults to column and has no `inline-flex`). The two public barrels export the SAME names by design; collapsing them would put DOM components on the mobile import graph, which the boundary rules forbid. See the header of design-system-native/src/variants.ts for the full rationale. One row for the one decision: it covers a match between a file on one side and the file at the same relative path on the other (EmptyState, Field, Input, index, variants, and the `useTheme` hooks the exact rule meets at its floor). A copy anywhere else, apps/mobile/src/components included, is judged normally.

apps/mobile/src/i18n/catalog.ts vs apps/web/lib/i18n/catalog.ts — the two surfaces' message catalogs, one decision whatever span the tokenizer matches as they grow. The match is the PluralMessage/Message type preamble, which both seams need and neither can import, plus each catalog's opening `'key': 'value',` rows: the tokenizer normalizes string literals, so rows of one shape are token-identical regardless of their copy. It is the structural identity of two data tables of one shape (one product, two surfaces; the i18n gate reads both with one set of rules), not a copied implementation. WHY IT CANNOT BE EXTRACTED, a property of the harness rather than of this file: every shared package source root — packages/contracts, packages/platform/*, packages/api, packages/design-tokens — is SEEDED, so `update` can never deliver a new export into an existing install; extracting the type would compile on a fresh scaffold and break `types` on every consumer who adopted the web i18n seam. 'De-duplicating' the rows would mean making the two surfaces' copy or key names differ to satisfy a tokenizer — divergence manufactured to defeat a detector. Through 2.0.4 this was three fingerprint rows (e83e21400fb2, f6a177d37c0d, 4f2c41321264), one per extent the span took.

apps/web/app/sign-in/sign-in-form.tsx vs apps/web/app/sign-up/sign-up-form.tsx — the two credential forms' RETURN statements, after everything extractable was extracted: the email/password pair and the pair-level alert live in sign-in/credential-fields.tsx, the page shell in sign-in/ceremony-shell.tsx, and the ceremony logic in @app/supabase (mfa-flow + verifyEnrolmentCode). What remains is <form> + <CredentialFields {...}/> + a submit Button + a crossing Link, which the two entrances of one ceremony render identically ON PURPOSE — and the tokenizer normalizes string literals, so the remaining difference (labels, testIDs, hrefs) does not register. Folding the form element itself into the shared component was tried on paper and rejected: it needs ten props, and the two ten-prop CALL SITES are then themselves a token-identical clone of the same length — the extraction relocates the fingerprint without removing it. The halves where drift would be dangerous (the submit handlers: non-enumeration, the AAL branch, the offered-enrolment phases) are distinct code and already share their machinery.
